Linkage table: long-format coefficient registry for Rceattle processes

Source: R/0-linkage_table.R
linkage_table.Rd

A linkage table is the unified data structure used to describe every estimated coefficient that connects a process (recruitment, natural mortality, growth, ...) to a covariate or stratum. Each row of the table corresponds to exactly one scalar coefficient (a beta) and identifies (a) which process and parameter it modifies, (b) which species/sex/age subset it applies to, (c) which column of the shared design matrix X it multiplies, and (d) its prior, bounds, link, and estimation phase.

Details

The motivation is that the historical Rceattle pattern of one wide parameter array per process (e.g. beta_rec_pars[nspp, n_env], M1_beta[nspp, nsex, n_env]) does not generalize cleanly across processes that need different stratifications. A long-format table grows only with the linkages the user actually requests, regardless of the underlying species/sex/age dimensionality.

This file defines the schema and basic helpers; user-facing formula-driven constructors live in R/0-build_linkage.R.

Developed by Grant Adams.
